items.stem: A customer is shouting and repeating themselves. What is the most effective first response?

options.text: Acknowledge their frustration and confirm you will help
options.rationale: Correct: acknowledgement lowers tension before problem-solving.
Interrupting during high emotion usually escalates the call.
An abrupt hold can feel dismissive and increase anger.
Telling someone to calm down commonly has the opposite effect.

items.explanation: Correct: acknowledging the emotion first is the core of de-escalation.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve first-contact resolution? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Having an accurate, searchable knowledge base
options.rationale: Correct: good knowledge lets agents resolve more on first contact.

options.text: Asking clarifying questions early in the call
options.rationale: Correct: understanding the real need avoids repeat contacts.

options.text: Closing tickets quickly before confirming a fix
options.rationale: Premature closure causes re-opens and lowers true resolution.

items.explanation: Correct: knowledge quality and good questioning both raise first-contact resolution.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: What does an SLA response target primarily commit the support team to?

options.text: A maximum time to acknowledge or begin work on a ticket
options.rationale: Correct: response targets set the time to respond, not necessarily to resolve.

options.text: A guarantee the issue is always the user's fault
A promise never to escalate tickets
options.rationale: Escalation is normal and compatible with SLAs.

options.text: A rule that tickets can never be closed
options.rationale: SLAs govern timing, not whether tickets close.

items.explanation: Correct: a response target commits the team to a time to respond.
